architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the low-drift acrylic-only outcome if the repeat-mean SI_15_60 is below 4.04%. This is below half of the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction, calculated as 9.51% * 0.8500 = 8.08%, and supports H-RESIN while falsifying H-CORE and H-DUAL at their registered formulation-level criteria.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: S1C39 is 15% acrylic-modified chemistry outside the previously measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family. However, M-HOLD-120 observes SI_15_60 directly in S1C39 and is not marked inadmissible by the advisory audit. No, the primary observable does not depend on a rheological regularity measured in the same chemistry family as S1C39. The result can therefore support only a candidate-specific, formulation-level thermal-hold-drift claim; it cannot establish transfer of the old temperature-response shape, reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity, or identify a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If repeat-mean SI_15_60 is below 4.04%, H-CORE is falsified and H-DUAL is falsified because low drift occurred with zero minor tackifier. If repeat-mean SI_15_60 is at or above 8.08%, H-RESIN is falsified; H-CORE and H-DUAL remain entangled. A result from 4.04% up to but below 8.08% is intermediate and does not decisively falsify any of the three registered hypotheses.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: If SI_15_60 is at or above 8.08% and thus falsifies H-RESIN, run S1C41::M-HOLD-120 to test whether adding the 5% minor-tackifier axis produces the low-drift regime predicted by H-DUAL. If SI_15_60 is below 4.04% and falsifies H-CORE and H-DUAL, run S1C39::M-SWEEP before making any temperature-response or absolute-viscosity-transfer claim.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Arithmetic mean across at least two independent preparations of SI_15_60 = 100 * (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, measured during the 120 C hold; repeat-level SI_15_60 values must also be reported.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C39::M-HOLD-120 directly measures the declared 120 C residence-time failure mode while isolating the acrylic-like axis. Its 8.08% linear-dilution prediction and 4.04% low-drift threshold are separated by more than the declared 2.00-percentage-point resolution. This makes it the strongest available probe of whether acrylic modification alone yields formulation-level superlinear drift suppression and whether a minor tackifier is required, without invoking an unsupported thermal-shape transfer or a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer. The Proposer's S1C41::M-HOLD-120 is in the stable deterministic top set and is a plausible mitigation test, but activating both modifier axes gives H-RESIN and H-DUAL the same low-drift prediction and does not answer the registered acrylic-only question. S1C39 removes the tackifier confound and directly separates H-RESIN from H-DUAL. I therefore accept the scientifically motivated departure from the aggregate VOI ranking; the reported ranking stability is sensitivity of the score, not confidence that its preferred hypothesis coverage is the right one.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: Original 120 C hold evidence covers only E1 and E5, each with one reported trajectory. The 15% acrylic level is a directional lower-bound design point, and the queried external-prior tables returned no additional rows.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The candidate changes chemistry and has no verified transfer of the unmodified-family thermal-response shape. This does not require extrapolation for directly measured SI_15_60, but any temperature-shape, reconstructed-viscosity, or absolute-level interpretation remains unsupported until a direct M-SWEEP is performed.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The declared discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points. The 8.08% versus 4.04% prediction gap is 4.04 percentage points, so it is nominally separable. Classification is prospectively based on the arithmetic mean across at least two independent holds, with all repeat-level values retained to expose discordance.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Preparation-state variability is material: E2 showed approximately 2.80-3.57-fold absolute-viscosity spread. The within-hold relative observable reduces sensitivity to absolute level but does not eliminate process-history effects, so preparation and hold histories must be controlled and recorded.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The shared local temperature-response regularity was measured in the original reactive PUR chemistry represented by E1, E2, and E3, with the E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation evaluated separately; the original hold evidence is limited to E1 and E5. The intended acrylic-like modification of the E2 anchor changes chemistry and therefore does not automatically remain inside the validated support. Its thermal-response shape must be checked directly rather than assumed transferable.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive, formulation-sensitive viscosity growth during prolonged melt residence at 120 C (thermal-hold drift).
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold showed SI_15_60 = 0.5154, corresponding to a 51.54% viscosity increase from 15 to 60 min at 120 C; by contrast, original E1 increased 9.51% over the same window.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local 120 C hold trajectories, each represented by one reported run with four points over 15-90 min. There are no independent hold repeats in the supplied local data. In contrast, temperature response was measured over 80-130 C for multiple formulations and runs, and realized viscosity level, although highly variable, was repeatedly observed for E2 with three runs at each temperature. Therefore the time-dependent drift coordinate has the sparsest replication and chemistry coverage.
measurement_requirements: Use the matched-window M-HOLD-120 protocol: hold at 120 C, measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage.
Run at least two independent preparations and holds so that a single realization or process history is not treated as the formulation response.
Record the candidate's reactive mass fraction phi_r and prospectively calculate the H-CORE prediction as 9.51% times phi_r.

Freeze the mechanistic decision thresholds before observing results: agreement with the linear-dilution prediction within the declared 2 percentage-point measurement resolution supports H-CORE, while drift below half the linear-dilution prediction supports H-RESIN; low drift without tackifier falsifies H-DUAL.
Because the acrylic-like modifier is outside the demonstrated shared-shape chemistry, include a fresh 80-130 C sweep in 10 C increments rather than relying only on one-point state calibration.

Measure and report absolute realized viscosity values in the source instrument units without inventing a unit, and preserve each preparation's process history so level displacement can be distinguished from hold drift.
planner.scientific_question: For an E2-anchored formulation with a nonzero acrylic-like fraction and zero minor tackifier-like fraction, is the matched-window 120 C viscosity drift consistent with the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction, or is it less than half that prediction as required by H-RESIN? A low-drift acrylic-only result would also falsify H-DUAL's claim that a minor tackifier is required.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is resin-modified chemistry outside the family in which the shared temperature-response shape was established. However, M-HOLD-120 directly measures matched-window drift and does not infer it from that shared shape, so the observable remains chemistry-applicable and is explicitly admissible under the advisory audit. Both intervention axes are within externally supported regions: 15% acrylic-like modifier is at the supported 15-25% boundary, and 5% minor tackifier lies in the repeated 4.8-6.4% cluster.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is below 3.80% across at least two repeats, it is below half of the 7.61% H-CORE linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000. This falsifies H-CORE at the registered criterion and supports superlinear resin-associated suppression. Because both modifier axes are active, the result remains compatible with both H-RESIN and H-DUAL and does not distinguish them.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result supports H-CORE's linear-dilution account. It also weighs against H-DUAL's predicted low-drift behavior when the minor tackifier axis is active.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.80% up to but below 7.61% would indicate suppression relative to linear dilution without meeting the registered superlinear-suppression threshold. It would not decisively support H-CORE or H-RESIN and would still leave H-RESIN versus H-DUAL unresolved.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly during a 120 C hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min across at least two independent repeats

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Identical deterministic information value and chemistry applicability, but requires a larger 22.5% total modifier burden without increasing hypothesis-pair separation.
Identical deterministic information value, but its 25% total modifier burden is a larger departure from the local reactive chemistry than S1C41.
Identical deterministic information value, but uses 27.5% total modifier and therefore makes a less minimal intervention.
Identical deterministic information value, but has the largest tied modifier burden at 30%, placing acrylic loading at the upper supported boundary without added discrimination.

Retains direct drift measurement and the same pairwise discrimination, but its 7.5% tackifier loading lies above the repeated 4.8-6.4% support cluster, producing nonzero extrapolation risk and a lower VOI score.

proposer.reasoning: M-HOLD-120 directly interrogates the declared failure mode and the least-resolved isothermal-time coordinate, rather than relying on a fitted thermal-response descriptor. S1C41 separates H-CORE from both low-drift alternatives with zero composition extrapolation risk, although it explicitly cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL. The choice is stable to all reported weight perturbations, and within the five-way top tie S1C41 is the minimum-burden, fully supported dual-axis intervention.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI components and directly separate the same two hypothesis pairs. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden among them—15% acrylic-like plus 5% tackifier-like—while keeping both axes inside their supported intervention regions. It therefore provides the same discrimination with the smallest justified departure from the characterized reactive chemistry.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Changed the primary experiment from dual-axis S1C41::M-HOLD-120 to acrylic-only S1C39::M-HOLD-120. The direct 120 C hold remains applicable to the modified chemistry, while S1C39 removes the tackifier confound and separates H-RESIN from H-DUAL. The chemistry-domain limitation does not invalidate this direct drift observable, but results must not be used to claim transferable temperature-response shape, reconstructed 120-130 C viscosity, or absolute-viscosity relocation without a direct M-SWEEP.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The proposal S1C41::M-HOLD-120 is in the five-card deterministic tied top set. However, the preferred experiment departs from that ranking because every tied-top card activates both modifier axes and leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled. S1C39::M-HOLD-120 is the acrylic-only card identified in the payload that directly answers the registered scientific question and separates the key H-RESIN versus H-DUAL pair. This is a scientific hypothesis-coverage reason not captured by the score's aggregate discrimination count, rather than a preference-based tie break.
residual_decision_risk: The protocol does not prospectively define aggregation of multiple repeats or classification when repeat values fall on opposite sides of a threshold.
Preparation and process-state variability remains material; process histories must be controlled and recorded so realization effects are not mistaken for formulation effects.
S1C39::M-HOLD-120 can separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL, but a near-linear result leaves H-CORE and H-DUAL observationally entangled.
The modified chemistry has no verified transfer of the unmodified-family thermal-response shape; temperature-response, reconstructed-viscosity, and absolute-level claims require a direct M-SWEEP.
A drift result supports or rejects formulation-level rheological predictions but cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency mechanism proposed in H-RESIN.
The acrylic evidence at 15% is directional lower-bound evidence whose literature fraction denominator has not been reverified.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is decisive for experiment selection. S1C41 contains both 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100, under which H-RESIN and H-DUAL make identical low-drift predictions, so the experiment cannot test whether tackifier is required. S1C39 has 15% acrylic-like modifier and zero minor tackifier and therefore tests the stated acrylic-only question: low drift would falsify H-DUAL's tackifier-required claim, whereas drift near the linear-dilution prediction would distinguish that outcome from H-RESIN's superlinear-suppression prediction. S1C39 still leaves H-CORE and H-DUAL entangled for a near-linear result, but it resolves the key pair that all five tied-top experiments leave unresolved.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No reported perturbation changes the tied top set: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, there are no flipped scenarios, and every recommendation_flip_boundary survives scaling each individual weight from 0.5 to 1.5. The base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower is 0.004583. Thus no weighting within the reported sweep makes the proposal cease to be top ranked. Weightings outside that sweep were not evaluated. The departure to S1C39 is nevertheless scientifically defensible because the score counts separated pairs without encoding that H-RESIN versus H-DUAL is the pair central to the stated acrylic-only question.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The S1C41 composition is outside the previously measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry family, but the primary SI_15_60 observable is measured directly at 120 C and does not reuse the unsupported shared thermal-response shape. It is therefore valid for the drift comparison. A direct S1C41::M-SWEEP from 80 to 130 C would be required before transferring the old thermal shape or making temperature-response and reconstructed-viscosity claims.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: M-HOLD-120 directly produces SI_15_60, so values at or above 7.61% and below 3.80% are measurable outcomes. The H-CORE versus low-drift prediction difference is 3.804 percentage points, above the declared 2.00-point resolution. Practical adjudication remains incomplete because the protocol does not define how multiple repeats are aggregated or classified when they fall on opposite sides of a threshold.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result could reject H-CORE but could not determine whether acrylic modification alone suppresses drift or whether the minor tackifier is required, so the central H-RESIN versus H-DUAL decision would remain unresolved.
objections.objection: The registered scientific_question asks about an E2-anchored composition with nonzero acrylic-like fraction and zero minor tackifier-like fraction, but S1C41 contains 15.0% AC1920 and 5.0% TK100. At S1C41, H-RESIN and H-DUAL both predict 3.804% drift, so their predicted separation is 0 percentage points. The claimed H-CORE separation is valid: 7.608% versus 3.804%, a 3.804-point difference exceeding the declared 2.00-point resolution. The Proposer correctly lists H-RESIN versus H-DUAL as unseparated, but the selected experiment therefore does not answer the stated acrylic-only scientific question or test whether low drift can occur without tackifier.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any attribution of suppression specifically to AC1920, specifically to TK100, or to a specialized division of labor between them would be unsupported.
objections.objection: S1C41 activates both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 changes from 0% to 15.0%, TK100 changes from 0% to 5.0%, and the reactive-core fraction falls to 0.8000. The linear-dilution comparator accounts prospectively for the reactive-mass change, but a low SI_15_60 still cannot be attributed separately to acrylic-like modification, tackifier-like modification, or their interaction. In particular, the proposed hold cannot distinguish H-RESIN's general resin-associated suppression from H-DUAL's tackifier-required suppression.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The drift measurement itself remains interpretable, but threshold classification could become discretionary for conflicting repeats.
objections.objection: The primary observable survives this attack surface. SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 during the same 120 C hold; it requires no thermal-shape fit, extrapolation, or imputation. However, the protocol does not specify how the two or more independent repeat values are combined or how discordant repeats are adjudicated when one crosses a threshold and another does not.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The 120 C matched-window drift claim remains supportable, but any claim about transferable temperature-response shape, reconstructed 120-130 C viscosity, or absolute viscosity relocation would be outside measured chemistry support.
objections.objection: S1C41 is correctly identified as modified_chemistry_unvalidated, but M-HOLD-120 directly measures drift and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape established on unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI material. Thus the primary drift observable is not invalidated by shape transfer. Nevertheless, the selected protocol omits the fresh 80-130 C M-SWEEP explicitly required by the planner for this acrylic-modified chemistry. The shared shape must not be used to interpret S1C41's temperature response or reconstruct its viscosity level until such a sweep verifies transfer.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The criteria can be met, but repeat-to-repeat disagreement could permit post hoc classification of the same data as falsifying, supporting, or intermediate.
objections.objection: The numerical falsification outcomes are physically attainable by the specified measurement: SI_15_60 can be observed at or above 7.61% to falsify H-RESIN, or below 3.80% to falsify H-CORE under the Proposer's stricter threshold. The 7.608-to-3.804 prediction gap exceeds the 2.00-point resolution. The practical weakness is that 'across at least two repeats' is defined for acceptance but no explicit rule states whether falsification requires every repeat, the repeat mean, or a confidence bound to cross 7.61% or 3.80%. Results straddling a threshold therefore lack a prospectively fixed decision rule.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A rheological threshold result could be overstated as proof of a unique molecular or encounter-frequency mechanism rather than evidence for a formulation-level drift pattern.
objections.objection: No direct use of an unmeasured S1C41 outcome is shown. The payload states that held-out validation identity and outcomes were excluded, although the exact current grid was formalized after the validation experiment and lacks a repository freeze artifact, which limits independent verification of prospective provenance without demonstrating actual leakage. On scope, M-HOLD-120 can adjudicate the registered formulation-level drift predictions, but it cannot establish the specific causal explanation in H-RESIN that suppression occurs by lowering effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species. It can show superlinear suppression phenomenologically, not identify that microscopic cause.

skeptic.recommended_change: Use the payload card S1C39::M-HOLD-120, which has 15% acrylic-like modifier and zero minor tackifier, as the primary test of the stated acrylic-only question; this can separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL. If resources permit full coverage, run it alongside S1C41::M-HOLD-120 and prospectively define repeat aggregation and discordance rules. Add S1C41::M-SWEEP only if temperature-shape transfer or absolute-viscosity relocation will be interpreted.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The selected dual-axis S1C41 experiment does not answer the stated acrylic-only scientific question and gives H-RESIN and H-DUAL identical 3.804% predictions, leaving the key tackifier-required alternative experimentally entangled.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This mandatory upstream audit is required before candidate or experiment ranking and is needed to establish the exact chemistry provenance, state-shift evidence, shared thermal-response support, hold contrast, and separate E1 +P perturbation evidence.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
